explanations.static: Deterministic static task in Taskflow (tf::Task). Executes procedural routines in C++20 with sequential or concurrent guarantees based on a dependency graph.
explanations.condition: Decision and conditional branching task (tf::Task returning int). Evaluates predicates at runtime to direct control flow to the corresponding branch.
explanations.switch: Multiway selection (tf::Task returning int). Chooses which path to follow among several cases: the C++ body returns the case index and each case is an output port. The last case is the "default": any out-of-range value goes to it.
explanations.mcp: Calls ONE tool of an MCP server of the project, with no AI model in between. The result is available to the following vertices (an agent, a switch...). It uses the native C++ MCP client, keeping the session open to be fast.
explanations.subflow: Dynamic hierarchical decomposition task (tf::Subflow). Instantiates and expands new child task graphs at runtime within the MSVC thread pool, enabling recursive parallelism.
explanations.module: Independent and reusable hierarchical module (tf::Task via tf.composed_of). Encapsulates another complete graph in a single structured vertex, promoting modular composition.
explanations.critical: Mutual exclusion critical section (tf::CriticalSection). Synchronizes access to shared resources and prevents race conditions among concurrent workflow tasks.
explanations.cuda: GPU-accelerated task (tf::cudaGraph / cudaGraphExec). Dispatches massively parallel processing flows directly to the video architecture under C++20.
explanations.fork: Concurrent dispatcher (tf::Task). Dispatches multiple parallel execution branches simultaneously in the pipeline (such as content generation and diagram compilation).
explanations.join: Synchronization and consolidation barrier (tf::Task). Strictly awaits the completion of all concurrent branches before proceeding to subsequent steps.
explanations.agent: AI Agent vertex with governance and sandbox. Operates with language models (Code Mode), MCP tools and container or microVM isolation permissions.
